Subject: Orchard hosted trial fit & access — quick recap and asks

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciate you and Liam taking the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can scope the hosted trial correctly: 

Recap
- Goal: embed a low-latency assistant into Orchard’s customer support flow (web chat + ticket summarization).
- Key constraints you called out: ~1.5k daily active users to start, spikes to ~200 concurrent chats for short bursts, average prompt length ~150 tokens, peak burst windows of ~10–15 minutes.
- Security: you mentioned SOC 2 is important; several customers keep PII in prompts but are comfortable with hosted if retention is configurable.

Recommended hosted quickstart (what Redwood can provision immediately)
- Sandbox endpoints (staging.redwood.ai) + short-lived API key for your SRE team.
- Default trial rate cap: 200 requests/minute (configurable) with token-based throttles. We can adjust after we see traffic.
- Endpoint mapping: Chat endpoint for live interactions, Batch/generate for ticket summarization.

Asks from your side (please confirm)
- Expected peak QPS during your busiest minute (estimate).
- Will you need VPC/private networking for the pilot, or is hosted SaaS acceptable for the demo customers?
- Any regulatory constraints (HIPAA/finance) that would force Private/Dedicated from day one?

Attachments I’ve included: your network diagram (you shared during the call) and our quickstart checklist for hosted trials. I’ll loop in Monica (solutions) for the technical call if you want deeper onboarding on endpoint mapping and caching.

If hosted looks acceptable, I propose we start the 2-week sandbox pilot the week of Aug 24 — Monica can run a short preflight with your SRE to verify egress/IP allowances and tokenization behavior.

Next steps
- Can you confirm peak QPS and whether you require VPC for the pilot?
- If yes to VPC/private, we’ll switch to a Dedicated/Private proposal and share a rough cost delta.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few answers and follow-ups: 

- Peak QPS: in a full support campaign we saw peaks around 6–7 QPS (~420 requests/min), though that was with simple intents. For richer generation (summaries + context), estimate ~3–4 QPS sustained in spike windows — say 300 requests/min as a safe pilot assumption.
- VPC/Private: for the MVP with a small set of pilot customers, our security team is OK with hosted if we can control retention and set short message retention windows. However, for enterprise customers (post-pilot) we’ll likely need Private VPC or Dedicated options.
- Compliance: no PHI; PII exists but we can pseudonymize before sending. SOC 2 is required and you mentioned Redwood is SOC 2 compliant — please confirm.

Two asks from us: 
1) Can you outline what the hosted trial token/rate limits look like in practice? e.g., how token throttling is applied vs request throttling; what happens if we exceed the cap during a burst?
2) Can Monica walk our SRE through the network egress pattern? I attached a network diagram (orchard_network_diagram.pdf) that shows our proxy layer — happy to get on a short call.

Also, cost ballpark: can you give a rough hosted vs dedicated delta for our expected pilot footprint? We just need directional numbers to make the pilot budget ask to finance.

Appreciate it — Samira

Date: 2026-08-19T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Orchard hosted trial fit & access — quick recap and asks

Samira — great, thanks for the details and for attaching the diagram. Quick answers inline and next steps.

On token vs request throttling
- Redwood enforces both a requests-per-minute cap and a token-rate ceiling. For the hosted trial we set a request cap (e.g., 300 req/min) and a token cap (e.g., 90k tokens/min) — the token cap prevents a few very long prompts from taking down the burst window.
- If you exceed the request cap: requests are rate-limited (429) with a short retry-after header. We also expose per-endpoint metrics in the Console so you can monitor.
- If you exceed the token cap: same behavior (429) but we return a token-usage breakdown so you can attribute spikes to generation vs context.

Hosted vs Dedicated cost delta (directional)
- Hosted (sandbox / trial): no setup fee, usage-only pricing. For your pilot footprint (est. 300 req/min with avg 150 tokens/request) we estimate ~X USD/day (I’ve put directional numbers in the HubSpot note).
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity. Expect a 2–3x higher baseline cost but much tighter SLOs and dedicated GPU pools suitable for sustained high QPS.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): larger one-time setup + monthly fee; recommended when you need private networking and strict data residency.

Recommended next steps
1) Monica to run a 45-min preflight with your SRE (network egress, allowed IPs, TLS/TLS intercepts). Proposed slots: Aug 20 or Aug 21, 09:00–11:00 PT.
2) We’ll provision sandbox API keys and an endpoint matrix for the pilot: chat.generate, chat.stream, and batch/summarize. I attached the endpoint_matrix.csv and redwood_quickstart_checklist.pdf with required firewall rules and header expectations.
3) We’ll set initial caps: 300 req/min and 90k tokens/min. We can bump these after the first 48 hours of telemetry.

Samira — is Aug 20 at 09:30 PT for a technical preflight with Monica workable? If yes we’ll send a calendar invite and sandbox keys the same day.

—Ben
